program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The node’s criterion already distinguishes complete from partial, but its question asks only whether a frog is inside, which can collapse that distinction and invite inconsistent labels. Align the question with the existing placement criterion: assess whether a frog is visibly within the toilet bowl (not merely on the lid or nearby), and reserve partial for ambiguous or only partly-in placement. In the edited image, one frog appears clearly inside the bowl; others are on the lid and floor, so those extras do not make the requested change partial. The traces mostly call this complete, with one partial trace despite describing the same clear placement and reporting 0.99 confidence. Investigate that criterion/label mapping and trace inconsistency rather than treating the aggregate reference as atomic ground truth. All traces are valid, queried, and dependency-free, so this is not a transport or schema failure.
